## Left open at serialize.java 2.1.0

Reference v2.1.0's uniform rules (IMPLEMENTING.md U1 to U16) and the 2026-10-27 audit findings for this port, deferred when the 2.1 wrap-up order (Glenn, 2026-10-27) limited 2.1.0 to the re-vendor and the rejected reason (U2, landed). Each rule is unaudited here until its item closes: none is claimed kept or broken.

### U1: write buffers are a multiple of 8 bytes

Check that WriteStream and BitWriter require and check (under -ea) a buffer length that is a multiple of 8, and that every doc says 8, never 4. Done when: a unit test cites U1 and is green, with a red-first test and fix if the port broke the rule, or a one-line note that the port already keeps it.

From: IMPLEMENTING.md U1 at mas-bandwidth/serialize v2.1.0; deferred by the 2.1 wrap-up order, 2026-10-27

### U3: the writer never sends bytes that differ from the caller's value

Check that string writes and measures use a strict UTF-8 encoder: a lone surrogate is write misuse and is never replaced with '?' or U+FFFD. Done when: a unit test cites U3 and is green, with a red-first test and fix if the port broke the rule, or a one-line note that the port already keeps it.

From: IMPLEMENTING.md U3 at mas-bandwidth/serialize v2.1.0; deferred by the 2.1 wrap-up order, 2026-10-27

### U4: check UTF-8 and NUL on every string write

Check that the checked (-ea) write path refuses unencodable text and U+0000 on string write and measure. Done when: a unit test cites U4 and is green, with a red-first test and fix if the port broke the rule, or a one-line note that the port already keeps it.

From: IMPLEMENTING.md U4 at mas-bandwidth/serialize v2.1.0; deferred by the 2.1 wrap-up order, 2026-10-27

### U5: int bounds are int32

Check that a min or max outside int32 is caught on write and measure, and refused as value_out_of_range on read; never a silent 0-bit field. Done when: a unit test cites U5 and is green, with a red-first test and fix if the port broke the rule, or a one-line note that the port already keeps it.

From: IMPLEMENTING.md U5 at mas-bandwidth/serialize v2.1.0; deferred by the 2.1 wrap-up order, 2026-10-27

### U6: a measure stream refuses nothing

Check that measure misuse follows the write-misuse mechanism (assert) and a measure never latches a read refusal. Done when: a unit test cites U6 and is green, with a red-first test and fix if the port broke the rule, or a one-line note that the port already keeps it.

From: IMPLEMENTING.md U6 at mas-bandwidth/serialize v2.1.0; deferred by the 2.1 wrap-up order, 2026-10-27

### U7: a reader never traps

Check that read-side caller misuse (negative byte count, string buffer size below 1, bad declarations) returns false with value_out_of_range rather than throwing, with the failure state checked first. See ledger items ledger-string-buffer-size and ledger-read-misuse. Done when: a unit test cites U7 and is green, with a red-first test and fix if the port broke the rule, or a one-line note that the port already keeps it.

From: IMPLEMENTING.md U7 at mas-bandwidth/serialize v2.1.0; deferred by the 2.1 wrap-up order, 2026-10-27

### U8: over-wide values on write are caught in the checked build

Check that a value that does not fit its bit width is caught under -ea rather than masked. Done when: a unit test cites U8 and is green, with a red-first test and fix if the port broke the rule, or a one-line note that the port already keeps it.

### U9: one write-misuse mechanism per implementation

Done when: a unit test cites U9 and is green, with a red-first test and fix if the port broke the rule, or a one-line note that the port already keeps it.

### Audit M: string read with bufferSize below 1 lets the wire pick a throw

A string read with bufferSize < 1 and wire length 0x80000000 throws NegativeArraySizeException, so the wire picks throw versus accept (U7). Reproducer: /Volumes/nova/ai/rowan/working/serialize-love/audit2/serialize.java/audit/Repro.java R1. Run it first and confirm it fails before fixing. Done when: the reproducer is a unit test that is red on the old code and green on the fix, refusing value_out_of_range.

### Audit L: USAGE.md says 8-byte slack; the reader pads a tail window and pays a per-read branch

USAGE.md documents an 8-byte read slack, but the BitReader pads a tail window and pays a branch per read, which IMPLEMENTING.md's buffer contract calls the slower correct option (speed rule). Same as serialize.js issue 22. Timing runs only on amd-3. Done when: the slack contract is measured against the zero-slack reader on amd-3, the faster one ships, and USAGE.md states the contract the reader actually has.

From: serialize-love AUDIT-LEDGER.md, heading java, 2026-10-27; deferred by the 2.1 wrap-up order

### Audit L: the hostile-read fuzzer has no negative control, no -da leg and a fixed bufferSize

The hostile-read fuzzer has no planted-defect negative control, runs only with assertions on, and uses one fixed string bufferSize. Done when: a planted read defect is caught by the hostile-read fuzzer in CI, a -da leg runs, and bufferSize is fuzzed.
